title: The Year of Less
author: Cait Flanders
thesisParagraph: A yearlong shopping ban becomes a pressure test for every habit that once softened discomfort: buying, drinking, eating, television, overwork, and aspirational clutter. Less consumption does not solve grief or uncertainty, but it removes the escape routes long enough for values, relationships, and self-trust to become visible again.

signatureMoves: uses memoir warmth, spending restraint, and emotional honesty about less
connects clutter, consumption, and coping without scolding the reader
keeps the tone intimate, practical, and quietly brave
turns subtraction into attention to what remains
structures the memoir as twelve monthly field reports with sober statistics and emotional aftershocks
avoidMoves: Avoid "The point is" as a paragraph hinge.
Avoid "the question is" as a setup crutch.
Avoid triadic abstract-noun lists such as clarity, courage, and resilience.
Do not make minimalism a purity contest.
Do not skip the emotional reason the purchase was tempting.
does not present minimalism as aesthetic purity or moral superiority
does not lean on academic studies, jargon, or a clinical voice

voiceSpecimens: You don't need a prettier version of more.
Less starts telling the truth when the purchase no longer gets to hide the feeling.
teachingArc: The early months convert the shopping ban from a budgeting tactic into an inventory of emotional coping: belongings, alcohol, breakups, friendships, and seasonal pressure expose where consumption had been doing hidden work. The middle months deepen the test through family upheaval, loneliness, self-care experiments, and revised rules that distinguish deprivation from intentional support. The final months turn the freed money, space, and attention into agency: travel, career change, moving, and a practical guide for choosing enough over accumulation.
forbiddenMoves: Do not turn less into lifestyle branding.
Do not shame ordinary comfort when the issue is avoidance.
